newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 18.

text.p: GTE Corp expects to show strong profit and revenue growth in 1997, the Wall Street Journal reported.
- Investor Marvin Davis raised his offer for Carter-Wallace Inc by $93 million to $928 million or $20 a share.
- Tele-Communications Inc got approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission to spin off its direct-broadcast satellite operations.
- U.S. regulators plan to cut international telephone rates.
- Shares of Deutsche Telekom AG are to start trading on Monday.
- The Pentagon chose Lockheed Martin Corp and Boeing Co to make demonstration models of the proposed Joint Strike Fighter.
- Textron Inc's Bell Helicopter and Boeing Co plan to make a commercial version of their Osprey military aircraft.
- Texaco Inc agreed to pay $176.1 million in a racial discrimination suit.
- Prudential Securities will pay $18 million to settle lawsuits regarding its involvement in the defunct Foundation for New Era Philanthropy.
- AMRE Inc said HFS Inc is obliged to help it find money to finance its operations.
- Time Warner Inc asked the Federal Communications Commission to deny MCI Communications Corp's application for a U.S. direct-broadcast satellite license.
- The former Sumitomo copper trader said his boss in 1985 was involved in his first unauthorized deal.
- N2K Inc hired record producer Phil Ramone to create a label connected to the Internet.
- About 12 companies are set to issue private high-yield debt totaling nearly $2.3 billion.
- Industrial output dropped 0.5 percent in October.
- Investors have lost millions of dollars since Ronald Perelman announced plans to rescue the floundering Marvel Entertainment Group Inc.
